Zebra Technologies Introduces KC401 Kiosk to Drive Smarter Self-Service Across Industries
New Android-based device empowers frontline teams by automating routine tasks, reclaiming critical labor capacity and elevating customer service
LINCOLNSHIRE, Ill.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Sep. 17, 2026-- Zebra Technologies Corporation (NASDAQ: ZBRA), a global leader in digitizing and automating workflows to enable intelligent operations, today announced the launch of the KC401 kiosk, purpose-built to handle routine inquiries, eliminating workflow bottlenecks, reducing queue times, and freeing up staff for higher-value customer and patient interactions.
This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260917768873/en/
Zebra Technologies launches the new KC401 self-service kiosk.
Featuring a 10-inch display, the KC401 delivers a superior self-service experience for customers and frontline workers across the retail, hospitality, manufacturing, and healthcare industries delivering faster and more responsive self-service workflows.”
“As customer expectations for speed and convenience continue to grow, self-service technology serves as a defining feature of the modern store and other environments,” said James Poulton, Senior Vice President, Enterprise Mobile Computing, Zebra Technologies. “The KC401 provides a versatile, reliable solution for organizations to deliver the seamless, intuitive self-service experiences that their frontline workers and those they serve expect.”
The KC401 expands Zebra’s comprehensive self-service portfolio, including kiosks, mobile computers, and multipurpose touchscreens. With the integration of solutions from Elo, now part of Zebra, the expanded portfolio provides organizations across industries with a wider selection of versatile, high-performance products tailored to match their unique workflows.
Overcoming Friction for a Better Shopping Experience
New analysis from Coresight Research indicates a significant challenge in the retail industry, with more than 60% of retailers reporting that shoppers struggle to find products and navigate their stores. The KC401 directly addresses these hurdles, providing a digital touchpoint for shoppers to access product information like checking prices or inventory availability, and even view item availability, through an endless aisle experience.
According to the research, self-service solutions free up the capacity of about four associates per store on average, equaling about 22% of front-of-store labor capacity. Retailers can then reallocate this valuable time to higher-value activities like merchandising, returns, and in-store customer assistance.
Built for Durability, Seamless Deployment Across Frontline Operations
From the warehouse to the store floor, the KC401 is built for high-traffic environments. It withstands rigorous daily use across retail, hospitality, manufacturing and healthcare.
Enhanced with an impact-tested, scratch-resistant display, the kiosk can withstand everyday bumps and taps that are common in industrial environments, like manufacturing and warehousing.
Additionally, IP65-sealing protects against dust and liquids, allowing for frequent cleaning where hygiene standards are required, like restaurant kitchens or healthcare facilities.
An optional specialized scanner can simplify hands-free scanning workflows, making price and inventory checks, loyalty identification, and product returns more seamless.
The KC401 kiosk is also optimized with Zebra DNA and its comprehensive software suite of capabilities which simplifies device setup, security, and management. Zebra customers currently using the CC6000 kiosk can maintain operational continuity as the KC401 uses the same mounting solutions and infrastructure, enabling a cost-effective upgrade of digital touchpoints with minimal disruption.
The Zebra KC401 provides frontline workers and those they serve with superior self-service experiences.
The new kiosk is built to withstand high-traffic use and frequent cleaning, making it ideal for a wide range of applications across retail, hospitality, manufacturing, and healthcare.
Organizations benefit from an easy, flexible installation functioning as a drop-in replacement for existing CC6000 customers.
TECHNOLOGIES?
Zebra (NASDAQ: ZBRA) provides the foundation for intelligent operations with an award-winning portfolio of connected frontline, asset visibility and automation solutions which empower our customers to deploy AI on the frontline. Organizations globally across retail, manufacturing, transportation, logistics, healthcare, and other industries rely on us to deliver outcomes today while driving innovation for what’s next. Together with our partners, we create new ways of working that improve productivity and empower organizations to be better every day. Learn more at www.zebra.com.

Zebra Technologies ((ZBRA)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Zebra Technologies delivered a notably upbeat earnings call, emphasizing record revenue, sharply higher earnings, and expanding margins. Management balanced this optimism with a frank discussion of memory supply risks, one‑time tariff benefits, and uneven regional performance, but reiterated confidence in structural demand drivers such as AI, machine vision, RFID, and healthcare.
Zebra reported quarterly sales above $1.5 billion, up 20.4% year over year and 9.2% on an organic basis. The performance exceeded the high end of guidance, signaling strong demand across its portfolio and effective execution despite supply chain complexities.
Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 27.7%, expanding 7.1 percentage points from a year ago, aided by a tariff recovery. Even excluding this $73 million benefit, margins improved by about 2 points, indicating underlying efficiency gains and better cost control.
Non‑GAAP diluted EPS came in at $6.35 for the quarter, a 76% increase versus last year. The figure was significantly above prior guidance, reflecting operating leverage from higher sales and margin expansion as well as disciplined expense management.
Adjusted gross margin rose roughly 540 basis points to 53.3%, driven largely by the IEEPA tariff recovery and favorable foreign‑exchange movements. While these one‑offs boosted profitability, management underscored that core margin improvement remains positive even without them.
The company raised full‑year sales growth guidance to 14%–16%, lifting the midpoint by 3 points, and now expects adjusted EBITDA margins of 23.5%–24%. Third‑quarter sales are projected to grow 17%–20%, with an EBITDA margin around 22%, supported by a strong backlog and recent momentum.
Year‑to‑date free cash flow reached $361 million, and full‑year free cash flow is expected to be at least $1 billion, implying roughly 100% conversion. Zebra repurchased $568 million of stock in the first half and plans around $150 million more in the second half, targeting about $700 million for the year.
Broad-Based End-Market and Regional Strength
End‑market demand was robust, with double‑digit growth in retail, manufacturing, and healthcare, the latter being the fastest‑growing sector. Regionally, North America grew 9%, EMEA 7%, Asia Pacific 13%, and Latin America 15%, underscoring a geographically diversified expansion.
Strategic Momentum in AI and Machine Vision
Zebra highlighted growing traction in AI‑powered frontline solutions and new AI‑optimized mobile devices. Machine vision outperformed expectations, helped by the Photoneo acquisition, while the Elo integration is driving early cross‑sell synergies estimated at about $10 million.
Supply-Chain Actions and Pricing Mitigation
The company has secured additional memory supply and fully offset a $20 million memory cost increase in Q2 through pricing and other actions. Expected pricing realization has been raised from roughly $60 million to $90 million to help counter an approximate $120 million memory headwind.
Management warned that memory supply remains dynamic and could constrain growth in the back half of 2026 and into 2027. Memory costs are expected to rise from Q2 to Q3, prompting continued mitigation efforts such as pricing adjustments, supplier qualification, and diversified sourcing.
A $73 million tariff recovery materially lifted Q2 gross margin and EBITDA, inflating reported profitability in the near term. Without this item, margin expansion is more modest, making clear that investors should adjust expectations for normalized performance in coming quarters.
Zebra guided Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin to around 22%, down from Q2 levels as the tariff refund rolls off and memory costs increase by roughly one point. The sequential step‑down highlights the impact of transient benefits and rising input costs on short‑term profitability.
Transportation and logistics sales were flat year over year, reflecting a tough comparison against strong prior‑year results. In EMEA, growth of 7% lagged other regions, with continued softness in the Middle East dampening overall momentum.
RFID revenue was flat in the quarter due to project timing and inherent deal volatility. Management still expects double‑digit RFID growth for the full year, but the Q2 performance underscores that individual project schedules can create near‑term swings.
Pricing Actions and Customer Sensitivities
The company has already implemented price increases to offset memory inflation and signaled that further actions may be needed. While necessary for protecting margins, these moves can be commercially sensitive and may face customer resistance if cost pressures persist.
Dependence on Multiple New Memory Suppliers
Zebra is qualifying many new memory suppliers and chip types, targeting five to seven qualified vendors per memory category. This diversification reduces single‑source risk but introduces execution challenges in ramping capacity and ensuring timely qualification through 2027.
Forward-Looking Guidance and Capital Strength
Looking ahead, management’s guidance assumes full mitigation of about $120 million in memory headwinds through pricing and operational actions. Strong free cash flow, modest net leverage around 1.9x, and ample credit capacity support ongoing investment, acquisitions, and share repurchases as Zebra pursues AI, machine vision, RFID, and healthcare growth.
Zebra’s latest earnings call painted a picture of a company firing on most cylinders, with record sales, surging EPS, and upgraded guidance. Investors must weigh the temporary nature of tariff benefits and ongoing memory‑related risks, but the underlying demand trends and strategic positioning suggest a favorable long‑term trajectory.

Zebra Technologies upgrades RFID readers with Impinj Gen2X technology
At the RAIN in Action Summit, the companies are illustrating how tags and readers with Gen2X support can improve reading performance in challenging real-world settings.
When Impinj introduced Gen2X – a standards-compatible enhancement to the RAIN RFID protocol that improves the performance of RFID solutions in real-world enterprise deployments – the company made it widely available to the RAIN industry, enabling manufacturers to add support to both new and already popular readers.
Today, Impinj has announced that intelligent operations leader Zebra is upgrading its portfolio of RFID handhelds, sleds, and fixed readers with support for Impinj Gen2X. Zebra is adding Gen2X support to improve handheld and overhead reading of hard-to-read items, boost the accuracy and speed of autonomous track-and-trace solutions in challenging conditions, and use RFID tags to help inhibit fraudulent items and returns.
At this week’s annual RAIN in Action Summit, Impinj and Zebra are demonstrating Gen2X performance on Zebra handheld devices, illustrating how tags and readers with Gen2X support can improve reading performance in challenging real-world settings. RFID tagging is now expanding into categories such as grocery, jewelry, health and beauty, and pharmaceuticals – product types that were historically difficult to tag and inventory, yet are important to achieving item-level visibility across enterprise operations.
Impinj developed Gen2X to address these real-world challenges and improve autonomous fixed reading solutions at enterprise scale, enabling reliable item visibility across small retail merchandise, densely packed items, and products containing liquids and metals. These innovations now support use cases ranging from supply chain traceability and overhead inventory visibility to self-checkout and loss prevention.
Extending RFID tagging to more items and use cases empowers enterprises to automate workflows using Physical Intelligence: the reliable realworld visibility enterprise AI systems need to see everything, waste nothing, and act instantly.
“As RAIN RFID adoption continues to scale across global enterprises, Zebra is focused on delivering innovations that improve real-world performance and usability,” states Chip Yager, vice president and general manager, Advanced Locationing Technology, Zebra Technologies. “By enabling Gen2X across our handhelds, sleds, and fixed readers, we’re helping customers achieve more reliable reads, faster inventory, and greater accuracy, especially in challenging environments.”
“Zebra was our first licensee for Gen2X, and we are excited to see this innovation expand across a wide range of Zebra handheld, sled, and fixed readers,” adds Gahan Richardson, executive vice president and general manager, Impinj. “Extending Gen2X across its portfolio, Zebra is helping enterprises obtain item-level visibility into a wider range of use cases, accelerating the adoption of RAIN RFID at scale.”
Zebra devices with Gen2X support are available now, including handhelds (MC33 family, TC22R, TC501, TC701), sleds (RFD40 family, RFD90 family), and fixed/overhead readers (FXR90, FX9600, FX7500, ATR7000). Gen2X capabilities will be available across Zebra’s RFID portfolio via seamless firmware upgrades.

Zebra Technologies launches the new KC401 self-service kiosk.
New Android-based device empowers frontline teams by automating routine tasks, reclaiming critical labor capacity and elevating customer service
LINCOLNSHIRE, Ill., September 17, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Zebra Technologies Corporation (NASDAQ: ZBRA), a global leader in digitizing and automating workflows to enable intelligent operations, today announced the launch of the KC401 kiosk, purpose-built to handle routine inquiries, eliminating workflow bottlenecks, reducing queue times, and freeing up staff for higher-value customer and patient interactions.
Featuring a 10-inch display, the KC401 delivers a superior self-service experience for customers and frontline workers across the retail, hospitality, manufacturing, and healthcare industries delivering faster and more responsive self-service workflows."
"As customer expectations for speed and convenience continue to grow, self-service technology serves as a defining feature of the modern store and other environments," said James Poulton, Senior Vice President, Enterprise Mobile Computing, Zebra Technologies. "The KC401 provides a versatile, reliable solution for organizations to deliver the seamless, intuitive self-service experiences that their frontline workers and those they serve expect."
The KC401 expands Zebra's comprehensive self-service portfolio, including kiosks, mobile computers, and multipurpose touchscreens. With the integration of solutions from Elo, now part of Zebra, the expanded portfolio provides organizations across industries with a wider selection of versatile, high-performance products tailored to match their unique workflows.
Overcoming Friction for a Better Shopping Experience
New analysis from Coresight Research indicates a significant challenge in the retail industry, with more than 60% of retailers reporting that shoppers struggle to find products and navigate their stores. The KC401 directly addresses these hurdles, providing a digital touchpoint for shoppers to access product information like checking prices or inventory availability, and even view item availability, through an endless aisle experience.
According to the research, self-service solutions free up the capacity of about four associates per store on average, equaling about 22% of front-of-store labor capacity. Retailers can then reallocate this valuable time to higher-value activities like merchandising, returns, and in-store customer assistance.
Built for Durability, Seamless Deployment Across Frontline Operations
From the warehouse to the store floor, the KC401 is built for high-traffic environments. It withstands rigorous daily use across retail, hospitality, manufacturing and healthcare.
Enhanced with an impact-tested, scratch-resistant display, the kiosk can withstand everyday bumps and taps that are common in industrial environments, like manufacturing and warehousing.
Additionally, IP65-sealing protects against dust and liquids, allowing for frequent cleaning where hygiene standards are required, like restaurant kitchens or healthcare facilities.
An optional specialized scanner can simplify hands-free scanning workflows, making price and inventory checks, loyalty identification, and product returns more seamless.
The KC401 kiosk is also optimized with Zebra DNA and its comprehensive software suite of capabilities which simplifies device setup, security, and management. Zebra customers currently using the CC6000 kiosk can maintain operational continuity as the KC401 uses the same mounting solutions and infrastructure, enabling a cost-effective upgrade of digital touchpoints with minimal disruption.
The Zebra KC401 provides frontline workers and those they serve with superior self-service experiences.
The new kiosk is built to withstand high-traffic use and frequent cleaning, making it ideal for a wide range of applications across retail, hospitality, manufacturing, and healthcare.
Organizations benefit from an easy, flexible installation functioning as a drop-in replacement for existing CC6000 customers.

Zebra reported quarterly sales above $1.5 billion, up 20.4% year over year and 9.2% on an organic basis. The performance exceeded the high end of guidance, signaling strong demand across its portfolio and effective execution despite supply chain complexities.
Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 27.7%, expanding 7.1 percentage points from a year ago, aided by a tariff recovery. Even excluding this $73 million benefit, margins improved by about 2 points, indicating underlying efficiency gains and better cost control.
Non‑GAAP diluted EPS came in at $6.35 for the quarter, a 76% increase versus last year. The figure was significantly above prior guidance, reflecting operating leverage from higher sales and margin expansion as well as disciplined expense management.
Adjusted gross margin rose roughly 540 basis points to 53.3%, driven largely by the IEEPA tariff recovery and favorable foreign‑exchange movements. While these one‑offs boosted profitability, management underscored that core margin improvement remains positive even without them.
The company raised full‑year sales growth guidance to 14%–16%, lifting the midpoint by 3 points, and now expects adjusted EBITDA margins of 23.5%–24%. Third‑quarter sales are projected to grow 17%–20%, with an EBITDA margin around 22%, supported by a strong backlog and recent momentum.
Year‑to‑date free cash flow reached $361 million, and full‑year free cash flow is expected to be at least $1 billion, implying roughly 100% conversion. Zebra repurchased $568 million of stock in the first half and plans around $150 million more in the second half, targeting about $700 million for the year.
Broad-Based End-Market and Regional Strength
End‑market demand was robust, with double‑digit growth in retail, manufacturing, and healthcare, the latter being the fastest‑growing sector. Regionally, North America grew 9%, EMEA 7%, Asia Pacific 13%, and Latin America 15%, underscoring a geographically diversified expansion.
Strategic Momentum in AI and Machine Vision
Zebra highlighted growing traction in AI‑powered frontline solutions and new AI‑optimized mobile devices. Machine vision outperformed expectations, helped by the Photoneo acquisition, while the Elo integration is driving early cross‑sell synergies estimated at about $10 million.
Supply-Chain Actions and Pricing Mitigation
The company has secured additional memory supply and fully offset a $20 million memory cost increase in Q2 through pricing and other actions. Expected pricing realization has been raised from roughly $60 million to $90 million to help counter an approximate $120 million memory headwind.
Management warned that memory supply remains dynamic and could constrain growth in the back half of 2026 and into 2027. Memory costs are expected to rise from Q2 to Q3, prompting continued mitigation efforts such as pricing adjustments, supplier qualification, and diversified sourcing.
A $73 million tariff recovery materially lifted Q2 gross margin and EBITDA, inflating reported profitability in the near term. Without this item, margin expansion is more modest, making clear that investors should adjust expectations for normalized performance in coming quarters.
Zebra guided Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin to around 22%, down from Q2 levels as the tariff refund rolls off and memory costs increase by roughly one point. The sequential step‑down highlights the impact of transient benefits and rising input costs on short‑term profitability.
Transportation and logistics sales were flat year over year, reflecting a tough comparison against strong prior‑year results. In EMEA, growth of 7% lagged other regions, with continued softness in the Middle East dampening overall momentum.
RFID revenue was flat in the quarter due to project timing and inherent deal volatility. Management still expects double‑digit RFID growth for the full year, but the Q2 performance underscores that individual project schedules can create near‑term swings.
Pricing Actions and Customer Sensitivities
The company has already implemented price increases to offset memory inflation and signaled that further actions may be needed. While necessary for protecting margins, these moves can be commercially sensitive and may face customer resistance if cost pressures persist.
Dependence on Multiple New Memory Suppliers
Zebra is qualifying many new memory suppliers and chip types, targeting five to seven qualified vendors per memory category. This diversification reduces single‑source risk but introduces execution challenges in ramping capacity and ensuring timely qualification through 2027.
Forward-Looking Guidance and Capital Strength
Looking ahead, management’s guidance assumes full mitigation of about $120 million in memory headwinds through pricing and operational actions. Strong free cash flow, modest net leverage around 1.9x, and ample credit capacity support ongoing investment, acquisitions, and share repurchases as Zebra pursues AI, machine vision, RFID, and healthcare growth.
Zebra’s latest earnings call painted a picture of a company firing on most cylinders, with record sales, surging EPS, and upgraded guidance. Investors must weigh the temporary nature of tariff benefits and ongoing memory‑related risks, but the underlying demand trends and strategic positioning suggest a favorable long‑term trajectory.

Extending RFID tagging to more items and use cases empowers enterprises to automate workflows using Physical Intelligence: the reliable realworld visibility enterprise AI systems need to see everything, waste nothing, and act instantly.

Zebra Technologies Announces Second Quarter 2026 Results
Delivers record performance with broad-based growth across segments and regions
Lincolnshire, Ill., August 4, 2026 — Zebra Technologies Corporation (NASDAQ: ZBRA), a global leader in digitizing and automating workflows to deliver intelligent operations, today announced results for the second quarter ended July 4, 2026.
•Net sales of $1,557 million; year-over-year increase of 20.4%
•Net income of $233 million and net income per diluted share of $4.85
•Non-GAAP diluted EPS increased year-over-year to $6.35
•Adjusted EBITDA increased year-over-year to $431 million
•Recorded IEEPA tariff recoveries of $73 million, of which $14 million received in the quarter
“Our record results reflect broad-based demand for our innovative solutions and excellent execution on our growth and profitability priorities. We delivered for our customers by leveraging our long-standing supplier relationships to support our growth," said Bill Burns, Chief Executive Officer of Zebra Technologies. "The momentum we see across our business underscores Zebra's position as the foundation for intelligent operations and frontline AI as customers digitize and automate environments."
"Our strong balance sheet and cash flow continue to provide significant financial flexibility, enabling us to invest for growth while returning more than $560 million to shareholders in the first half of the year through disciplined share repurchases," said Nathan Winters, Chief Financial Officer of Zebra Technologies. "We believe this balanced approach positions Zebra to create long-term shareholder value."

Second Quarter 2026 Compared to the Second Quarter 2025
Net sales were $1,557 million compared to $1,293 million in the prior year. Net sales in the Connected Frontline ("CF") segment were $903 million compared to $717 million in the prior year. Asset Visibility & Automation ("AVA") segment net sales were $654 million compared to $576 million in the prior year. Consolidated organic net sales increased 9.2% year-over-year, with a 7.5% increase in the CF segment and an 11.4% increase in the AVA segment.
Gross profit was $825 million compared to $616 million in the prior year. Gross margin increased to 53.0% compared to 47.6% in the prior year primarily due to IEEPA tariff recoveries and favorable foreign currency exchange. Adjusted gross margin was 53.3% compared to 47.9% in the prior year.
Operating expenses increased to $504 million from $433 million in the prior year primarily due to expenses associated with acquired businesses including amortization of intangible assets. Adjusted operating expenses increased to $419 million from $370 million in the prior year.
Net income was $233 million, or $4.85 per diluted share, compared to net income of $112 million, or $2.19 per diluted share, in the prior year. Non-GAAP net income increased to $305 million or $6.35 per diluted share, compared to $186 million, or $3.61 per diluted share for the prior year.
Adjusted EBITDA increased to $431 million, or 27.7% of adjusted net sales, compared to $267 million, or 20.6% of adjusted net sales in the prior year.
As of July 4, 2026, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $157 million and total debt of $2,776 million.
For the first six months of 2026, net cash provided by operating activities was $387 million and the Company invested $26 million in capital expenditures, resulting in free cash flow of $361 million. The Company also made share repurchases of $568 million.
Mr. Burns added, "Strong demand momentum and progress on productivity and memory supply supports our significantly increased outlook for the full year. We are focused on driving sustainable growth across our business with our innovative portfolio of solutions, as we continue to benefit from trends in automation and Physical AI."
The Company expects third quarter sales growth between 17% and 20% compared to the prior year. This expectation includes approximately 10.5 points of favorable impact from business acquisitions, dispositions and foreign currency.
Adjusted EBITDA margin for the third quarter is expected to be approximately 22%. Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share are expected to be in the range of $4.70 to $4.90. This assumes an adjusted effective tax rate of approximately 19%.
The Company expects full year sales growth between 14% and 16% compared to the prior year. This expectation includes approximately 8 points of favorable impact from business acquisitions, dispositions and foreign currency.
Adjusted EBITDA margin for the full year is expected to be between 23.5% and 24.0%. Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share are expected to be in the range of $20.75 to $21.25. This assumes an adjusted effective tax rate of approximately 19%.
Free Cash Flow for the full year is expected to be greater than $1 billion.
